thread.title: Apple taps A24 for movie slate

author: Annlee Ellingson
title: Apple taps A24 for movie slate
text: – Staff Writer, L.A. Biz Nov 15, 2018, 2:34pm PST Apple Inc. has made its first major move into the movie space with a multiyear deal with A24, the New York-based independent film distribution and production company behind the Oscar-winning “Moonlight” and box-office hit “Hereditary.” Under the agreement, A24 will produce multiple titles for the computer giant. Little else, including terms, is known about the deal, such as whether the films will play in theaters, a la Amazon’s model, or almost exclusively online, like Netflix’s. Launched in 2012, A24 is a hot new distributor, with such films as “Spring Breakers,” “Ex Machina,” “Room,” “The Witch” and the documentary “Amy.” Its recent films include “Mid90s” and “Eighth Grade.” The company already has distribution deals with DirecTV and Amazon Prime, but the Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) agreement puts A24 in business with a tech giant eager to make up lost ground to Netflix and Amazon. There were even rumors that Apple would acquire a small movie studio, including A24. Apple has committed an initial $1 billion for series content for its forthcoming digital video platform, which has signed content deals with Oprah Winfrey and Sesame Workshop and is working on series including “Amazing Stories,” a drama about a morning news show starring Jennifer Aniston and Reese Witherspoon, and a thriller from M. Night Shyamalan, among other projects. Apple’s worldwide video programming is led by Jamie Erlicht and Zack Van Amburg, whom the company poached from Sony last year, though it has yet to announce any splashy film hires.
